todays_goal: Advance from equivalent expressions into one-step equations while retrieving two precision rules.

lessons.subject: mathematics
lessons.previous_learning: Day 19 showed strong repair of the distributive property and strong combining-like-terms work. Precision issues remain with signed terms and the equals-sign definition of equation.
lessons.course_context: Brief precision retrieval, then introduce solving one-step equations with inverse operations.
learning_objectives: Solve addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division equations.
lessons.why_it_matters: Equations model unknown quantities and are foundational for later algebra.

vocabulary.definition: a statement with an equals sign showing two quantities are equal
a value that makes an equation true
an operation that undoes another operation

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: solving an equation means finding the value that makes both sides equal. Use the inverse operation on both sides, then check your solution.

worked_examples.title: Addition
worked_examples.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides and check 12+7=19.

exit_ticket.prompt: What does it mean to check a solution?
exit_ticket.answer: Substitute it back into the original equation and verify both sides are equal.

lessons.voice_prompt: Use a balance model on the whiteboard. Keep prompts short. Ask Atticus which operation is attached to the variable and what inverse operation undoes it. Never give an assigned final answer. Require a substitution check on exit-style problems.
lessons.teacher_notes: Advance from distributive property; signed-term and equation-definition retrieval remains brief.
